title: Structure and Liftoff In Combustion Experiment

sources.title: Structure and Liftoff In Combustion Experiment
A Computational and Experimental Study of Coflow Laminar Methane/Air Diffusion Flames: Effects of Fuel Dilution, Inlet Velocity, and Gravity

key_findings: The structure and stability of laminar diffusion flames in microgravity are significantly influenced by burner diameter, coflow velocity, and fuel composition.
Flames observed in microgravity are fundamentally different than those observed on Earth.
More than 4,000 high-resolution images were captured across 13 testing experiments.
fields.earth_applications: Improved numerical models for flame behavior lead to more efficient combustion technologies on Earth.

paper_findings.text: The flames become longer and wider as buoyancy is eliminated or fuel concentration is increased.
The computed temperature profiles and measured soot temperatures are modeled accurately.
The influences of varying inlet velocity are correctly captured.

conditions.label: CH4-air diffusion flames, normal gravity (1g)
evidence: Eighteen flames have been studied under both microgravity (μg) and normal gravity (1g) (36 flames total): three fuel dilution levels (40%, 70%, and 100% CH4 in mole fractions) and six inlet velocities (approximately 24, 46, 55, 64, 80, 89 cm/s, changing slightly at different fuel dilutions)

key_findings: The flames become longer and wider as buoyancy is eliminated or fuel concentration is increased.
The computed temperature profiles and measured soot temperatures are modeled accurately.
The influences of varying inlet velocity are correctly captured.
